reason: Moses and Aaron (the priestly figures in this passage) are depicted as faithful servants of God who obey His commands and serve as instruments of His divine power through the plagues. Although they face harsh criticism from both the Israelites (who blame them for worsening their situation) and opposition from Pharaoh, God consistently validates and reassures them, ultimately vindicating their mission. The narrative arc presents them as righteous and chosen despite their trials, establishing them as God's agents whose words and actions carry divine authority. The reader is positioned to view their faithfulness favorably, even amid the external criticism they endure.
